title: Beef and Broccoli
subtitle: Takeout vibes, hall timing
description: Takeout vibes, hall timing. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

steps.title: Slice and marinate beef
steps.instruction: Start the rice: rinse, then simmer covered with 4½ cups water and a pinch of salt 18 minutes; rest 5 minutes and fluff. Slice flank steak thin against the grain. Toss with 2 tbsp of the soy sauce, 1 tbsp cornstarch, and 1 tbsp oil; rest 15 minutes. Whisk the remaining soy sauce, oyster sauce, brown sugar, broth, ginger, and remaining cornstarch into a sauce.

steps.title: Stir-fry beef in batches
steps.instruction: Heat wok or large skillet until smoking with 1 tbsp oil. Sear beef in single layers 1–2 minutes until edges char, adding oil between batches; remove.

steps.title: Char broccoli
steps.instruction: Stir-fry broccoli in two batches with the remaining oil, 2 minutes until charred at the edges, then add 2 tbsp water and cover 1 minute until bright green and crisp-tender. Return all broccoli and beef, add garlic for 30 seconds, then pour in the sauce and toss 1–2 minutes until it bubbles and turns glossy.

steps.title: Serve over rice
steps.instruction: Serve Beef & Broccoli immediately over steamed rice — the sauce tightens if it sits.

proTips: Prep all mise en place before the bell — this meal wins on organization, not speed hacks.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Beef and Broccoli with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Beef and Broccoli on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Takeout vibes, hall timing. A hall pick for tight shifts — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Minimal prep — chop aromatics before shift change so you can cook as soon as the board quiets.

adaptable.label: Gluten-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use tamari (check soy-free brands separately) or coconut aminos. Use a certified gluten-free or vegetarian 'oyster' sauce alternative. Use a certified gluten-free broth or bouillon.
